In [[mathematics]], a '''closed preordered set''' is one whose anti-[[well-order]]ed subsets have [[lower bound]]s.

== Definition ==
Let <math>\kappa</math> be a cardinal. A [[preordered set]] <math>(P,\lesssim)</math> is called '''<math>\kappa</math>-closed''' if every subset of <math>P</math> whose [[converse relation|opposite]] is well-ordered with order-type less than <math>\kappa</math> has a lower bound.<ref name="Kunen"/>{{rp|214, Definition VII.6.12}}<ref name="Jech">{{cite book |last1=Jech |first1=Thomas |title=Set theory |language=en |edition=3 |series=Springer Monographs in Mathematics |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin |date=2003 |isbn=978-3-540-44085-7 |issn=1439-7382 |doi=10.1007/3-540-44761-X |mr=1940513 |zbl=1007.03002}}</ref>{{rp|Definition 15.7}}<ref name="Kurilić">{{cite journal|date=2025 |doi=10.1016/j.apal.2025.103567 |first=Miloš S. |issn=0168-0072 |issue=6 |journal=Annals of Pure and Applied Logic |language=en |last=Kurilić |mr=4874856 |pages=Paper No. 103567 |title=Iterated reduced powers of collapsing algebras |volume=176 |article-number=103567 |zbl=08018530}}</ref>{{rp|§2}}

A preordered set is '''<math>{<}\kappa</math>-closed''' if it is <math>\lambda</math>-closed for every <math>\lambda<\kappa</math>. A preordered set is called '''closed''' or '''<math>{<}{\operatorname{Ord}}</math>-closed''' if it is <math>\kappa</math>-closed for every <math>\kappa</math>.<ref name="FW">{{cite journal |last1=Freire |first1=Alfredo Roque |last2=Williams |first2=Kameryn J. |title=Non-tightness in class theory and second-order arithmetic |language=en |journal=The Journal of Symbolic Logic |volume=90 |issue=2 |pages=627–654 |date=2025 |issn=0022-4812 |doi=10.1017/jsl.2023.38 |zbl=08069454 |arxiv=2212.04445}}</ref>{{rp|Lemma 4.0.10}}

A preordered set is '''inductive''' if every [[chain (order theory)|chain]] has an upper bound. Since every totally ordered set has a well-ordered [[cofinal subset]], this is equivalent to saying that the preordered set is the opposite of a closed preordered set.

== Properties ==
Inductive preordered sets satisfy [[Zorn's lemma]] and the [[Bourbaki–Witt theorem]].

A <math>\kappa</math>-closed [[forcing (mathematics)|forcing]] preserves cofinalities less than or equal to <math>\kappa</math>, hence cardinals less than or equal to <math>\kappa</math>.<ref name="Kunen">{{cite book|title=Set theory: an introduction to independence proofs|last=Kunen|first=Kenneth|author-link=Kenneth Kunen|publisher=North-Holland|date=1980|isbn=978-0-444-86839-8|series=Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics|volume=102|zbl=0534.03026|mr=597342|language=en}}</ref>{{rp|215, Corollary 2.6.15}}
